target_customer: Engineering teams that want production debugging and observability at lower cost than Datadog
problem: Traditional observability vendors are expensive and split logs, metrics, traces and session replays across tools, slowing engineers who debug production issues.
business_model: Open core: MIT licensed open source plus a paid hosted cloud

founders.name: Warren Lee
previous_startups: A profitable company built from zero to millions in ARR (name not given)

competitors.name: SigNoz
competitors.what: Open source Datadog and New Relic alternative
competitors.traction_then: Had a Show HN launch; YC company

technical_complexity.rationale: Correlating logs, traces, metrics and session replay on top of ClickHouse is standard data engineering with hard performance parts for a team of four.

defensibility.rationale: Open source and built on a third party database, so rivals could replicate it; advantage was cost and developer experience.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ClickHouse, whose database the product ran on, acquired it in March 2025 and kept the cloud and open source project running.

market_need_then: Vendor cost was the stated driver, with the company claiming about ten times savings over Datadog. No dated third party spend data found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and developer focused, leading with price claims such as 10x cheaper than Datadog

branding.brand_signature: Open source and 10x cheaper than Datadog positioning

rebrands.why: Relaunched with ClickHouse as ClickStack after the acquisition; the repo README references the rename

branding.community_and_virality: Open GitHub project with roughly 9,600 stars in one snapshot of unknown date, an active Discord, and a Show HN post.

brand_strength.rationale: Healthy open source and Discord community and a clear cost position, but no press on the brand itself and the name was folded into ClickStack.

outcome_analysis: HyperDX built open source observability on ClickHouse and won a following of developers and early customers such as Lovable, plus ClickHouse itself as a user. The database vendor acquired it in March 2025, framing it as an acceleration, with deal terms undisclosed. Funding is unverified, so how capital efficient the path was cannot be stated.
notes: Acquisition date: the HyperDX blog is dated 2025-03-06 and ClickHouse and Business Wire dated 2025-03-13. Funding unverified: aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked) say about 500K with YC, Pioneer Fund, Race Capital and ClickHouse; not recorded as rounds. SigNoz Show HN date inferred as 2022, not confirmed. Completeness pass: The 2022-01 accelerator round (125K) rests on a single database (PitchBook); the 2022-09 seed is dated by VCBacked with no amount. Total of 500K (CB Insights, VCBacked) and 2.1M (Startups.fm) conflict and are not summed.
